title: Partnerships | Bridges Industrial
description: A vetted network of vendors, integrators, and specialists. Co-selling, bulk procurement, and referral partnerships that give clients more than any one company can.
html:
02 Partnerships

Alliances that move work, not just paper.

No single shop does everything well. We build a vetted network of vendors, integrators, and specialists, so a client gets the right team for the job instead of whoever happened to answer the phone. You bring the strength, we bring the reach.

/ What it brings

One relationship, a whole bench

Partnering with Bridges Industrial plugs you into capability, procurement, and demand you would not reach alone.

/ 01

Vendor Network

A bench of trusted instrument, controls, and software vendors, so the right specialist is always one introduction away.

/ 02

Bulk Procurement

Pooled buying power on hardware and licenses, so smaller shops get pricing usually reserved for the big accounts.

/ 03

Co-Selling & Referrals

We send work your way and you send it ours. Aligned incentives, clear terms, no poaching, no games.

/ 04

Integration Partners

Build on PragOptics: publish your own connections and apps on the platform, plug into our automation stack, and ship something real together.

/ 05

Vetted Quality

Everyone in the network is checked. A referral from us is a reputation we are putting on the line, so we mean it.

/ 06

Shared Standards

Common documentation, hand-off, and audit habits across the network, so the client experience stays consistent.

/ How it works

Simple, clear, and fair

STEP 01

Introduce

Tell us what you do well and who you serve. We get to know your work.

STEP 02

Vet

A quick, honest check on quality and fit, both directions.

STEP 03

Align

Clear terms on referrals, pricing, and how we represent each other.

STEP 04

Build

Real projects, shared wins, and a relationship that compounds.

Let's build a network

Strong companies, pointed in the same direction.

If you do good work and want more of it, let's talk. We would rather grow a bench than fight over a single job.
